scope: 17 conference papers on serving, scheduling, queueing and workload evaluation; complementary to MoE and architectural groups. No GPU work for this review.
evidence_policy: Full methods and evaluation sections read. Accessible author versions are distinguished from confirmed proceedings identity. Uncertainty not reported is not inferred. Source maxima retain their original baseline and measurement/simulation scope.

citation_graph.method: One backward/forward step through OpenAlex, plus primary references; metadata results manually screened.
citation_graph.integration: Splitwise forward neighborhood supplied DynamoLLM/BurstGPT; AlpaServe and ServerlessLLM references expose gamma/function-trace lineage. Off-topic metadata links discarded; no citation count used as evidence quality.

papers.doi_provenance: No DOI listed on the retrieved publisher proceedings page; no DOI inferred
papers.hypothesis: Iteration-level scheduling can avoid waiting for whole requests to finish.

papers.limitations: Synthetic lengths and dummy-weight workload cannot establish content-dependent MoE routing generality.

artifact.inspection: No public implementation inspected; later papers reimplement Orca.

papers.support_section_table_page: §§3–4 methods; §6 evaluation, PDF pp.11–15; engine and end-to-end figures.

burstgpt.static_defect: CSV iterator converts cumulative timestamps into successive gaps, but runner starts all tasks concurrently and sleeps each gap from task start. For timestamps [0,1,2], intended release offsets [0,1,2] become sleeps [0,1,1].
burstgpt.scope: Static inspection of this current example only; does not establish KDD25 implementation behavior. No network benchmark was run.
burstgpt.safe_use: Reuse raw pinned data with an independent absolute-clock replay contract and golden timestamp fixture.
